text: He won. Police in that city can no longer arrest on a face match alone. One town over, the rule does not exist.
provenance: Police there can no longer arrest anyone on a face-match alone.
Those rules bind one police department, in one city. Everywhere else, this same power still works the way it always has.

text: He was not the first. Before his story broke, at least two other men had already been arrested this exact way, one in the same city, one two states away.
provenance: Before his story ever broke, at least two other men — one in the same city, one two states away — had already been arrested this exact way, their cases only surfacing later.

text: And he was not the last. One woman was eight months pregnant, held in a cell over a crime a computer had tied to her face.
provenance: One of them was eight months pregnant — held in a cell over a crime a computer had tied to her face.

text: The group that represented him counts more than a dozen known wrongful arrests like his. Nearly every person named in them has been Black.
provenance: By the count of the group that represented him, there are now more than a dozen known wrongful arrests like his in this country, and nearly every person named in them has been Black.

text: Each of the others was an ordinary person, matched by a machine, believed over their own flat denial.
provenance: Each one an ordinary person. Each one matched by a machine. And each one believed over their own flat denial.

text: The city he sued was forced to rewrite its rules. A match is now a lead and nothing more.
provenance: As part of that deal, the city was forced to rewrite its rules.
The match is treated as a lead and nothing more.

text: Every earlier arrest made with the software has to be pulled and reviewed, going back years.
provenance: Every earlier case where the software was used to make an arrest has to be pulled and reviewed, going back years.

text: One man got a rule. Everyone else got a warning. And the rule only exists because his story got loud enough.
provenance: He was only the first whose story got loud enough to force anyone to change a single rule.
